nodes.question: What is the role of mobile capital in the model discussed?
nodes.answer: Mobile capital is used to produce goods, which are internationally tradable, for both polluting and environmental firms.
nodes.paragraph: This result is derived from a general equilibrium model in which policy decisions are made under international trade and capital mobility. The model includes perfectly competitive polluting firms and imperfectly competitive environmental firms. Whereas polluting firms produce a consumption good, environmental firms produce a good used for pollution abatement. Mobile capital is used to produce these goods, which are internationally tradable. Polluting firms purchase the environmental good to reduce their emissions and tax burdens.8 Capital mobility has been allowed for in studies on non-cooperative environmen- tal policies, such as Eichner and Runkel (2014), Tsakiris et al. (2018), Yamagishi (2019), and Eichner and Pethig (2019). Among these studies, Tsakiris et al. (2018) and Yamagishi (2019) consider pollution abatement; whereas Tsakiris et al. (2018) analyze public abatement, Yamagishi (2019) examines the case in which pollution abatement is set only by polluting firms. Unlike these studies, this paper introduces mobile capital into a model with an independent environmental sector. 6 When environmental goods are traded across (asymmetric) countries, environmental policies are used to improve the terms of trade.

nodes.question: Who supports the view that private corporations should play a leading role in sustainable development?
nodes.answer: The World Economic Forum (WEF) and its chairman Klaus Schwab support this view.
nodes.paragraph: 2020). The multi-stakeholder approach was also promoted by powerful business associa- tions, most prominently the World Economic Forum (WEF) through its Global Redesign Initiative, reflecting a broader vision of stakeholder capitalism (Canfield et al. 2021). nodes.question: What is the main focus of the review discussed in the abstract?
nodes.answer: The review focuses on the role of alternative currencies within the concept of degrowth and their interaction with societal changes and technological advancements.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract In this review, we analyze the existing literature on the role of alternative currencies within degrowth. While degrowth emerged in the early 2000s alongside growing awareness of accelerating environmental crises and widening global inequali - ties, alternative currencies have a longer history. Alternative currencies have served as devices for communities seeking to become less dependent on the dominant economic system, but degrowth and technological advancements are potentially reshaping alternative currencies, both in what their purpose could be and in how they operate. When combined with degrowth, these currencies are often expected to foster greater resilience at the local level and slow down the pace of socio-ecological metabolism. Building on our review, we propose a research agenda that explores how policy proposals and concepts such as universal basic income, localization, and entropy can be understood in relation to alternative currencies. Our main contribu- tion is to identify points of convergence and tension between alternative currencies and degrowth while proposing prospective research questions to guide future studies. Keywords Alternative currencies Complementary currencies Local currencies Social currencies Local exchange trading systems LETS Localisation Degrowth Cryptocurrencies Digital currencies Blockchain Introduction In addition to the acceleration of the environmental crisis on a global scale with consequences like climate disrup- tion, loss of biodiversity, increasing pollution, etc.

nodes.question: What is the main focus of the research conducted on SMEs in Lagos, Nigeria?
nodes.answer: The research focuses on exploring the sustainability and circular economic practices of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Lagos, investigating their experiences and challenges in implementing these practices.
nodes.paragraph: This paper therefore seeks to explore sustainabili - ity and circular economic practices of SMEs in Lagos Nigeria. Lagos State was selected as the appropriate location for the research because it is the most populous city in Nigeria, and at present Lagos State is currently experiencing challenges with the waste management systems in operation. The research investigates the expe - riences and challenges faced by SMEs as they seek to navigate the implementation of circular economy and environmental sustainability practices. In particular, the study seeks to assess the following: 1. SMEs perception and experience of challenges to the effective adoption of environmental sustainability and circular economic activities. 2. Role of SMEs in disseminating knowledge and infor - mation of environmental sustainability and circular economic activities to customers and the wider soci - ety. 3. Strategies to improve SME active engagement with environmental sustainability and circular economic activities. Circular economy and sustainability The circular economy, incorporates sustainable strate - gies to encourage recycling, promote sustainable use of natural resources, by engaging in smarter product design, to maximize the value of materials, products and services, minimize the use of virgin materials, reduce waste and develop new products and services compatible with the environment thereby regener - ating nature by tackling the problems of pollution, climate change and loss resulting from biodiversity (European Academies Science Advisory Council, 2015; UNDP , 2023).

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the study analyze sustainable finance research?
nodes.answer: The study analyzes sustainable finance research using big data analytics and machine learning on scholarly research.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Sustainable nance is a rich eld of research. Yet, existing reviews remain limited due to the piecemeal insights offered through a sub-set rather than the entire corpus of sustainable nance. To address this gap, this study aims to conduct a large-scale review that would pro- vide a state-of-the-art overview of the performance and intellectual structure of sustainable nance. To do so, this study engages in a review of sustainable nance research using big data analytics through machine learning of scholarly research. In doing so, this study unpacks the most in uential articles and top contributing journals, authors, institutions, and countries, as well as the methodological choices and research contexts for sustainable nance research. In addition, this study reveals insights into seven major themes of sustainable nance research, namely socially responsible investing, climate nancing, green nancing, impact investing, carbon nancing, energy nancing, and governance of sustainable nancing and investing. To drive the eld forward, this study proposes several suggestions for future sustainable nance research, which include developing and diffusing innovative sustainable nancing instruments, magnifying and managing the pro tability and returns of sustainable nancing, making sustainable nance more sustainable, devising and unifying policies and frameworks for sustainable nance, tackling greenwashing of corporate sustainability reporting in sus- tainable nance, shining behavioral nance on sustainable nance, and leveraging the power of new-age technologies such as arti cial intelligence, blockchain, internet of things, and machine learning for sustainable nance.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What challenge does the literature on sustainable finance currently face as observed in the recent review by Cunha et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: The literature on sustainable finance is excessively fragmented, making it difficult to identify what constitutes the field and how it differentiates from traditional finance.
nodes.paragraph: This calls for a broader and more encompassing de nition that speaks to sustain- ability at large. In this regard, we propose that sustainable nance should encompass all activities and factors that would make nance sustainable and contribute to sustainability , a de nition that we opine complements the myriad goals by different stakeholders, such as the European Commission S ESG and the United Nations SDGs. Indeed, the attainment of sustainable policy objectives across numerous jurisdictions can be achieved through various ways such as climate nance, carbon and ESG disclosure, green bonds, and socially respon- sible investment (Alsai et al., 2020 ; Barua & Chiesa, 2019 ; Lokuwaduge & Heenetigala, 2017 ; Migliorelli, 2021 E C D , 2020 Widyawati, 2020 ), all of which can be covered under our umbrella de nition of sustainable nance. Considering the broad nature of sustainable nance and its importance for achieving the sustainability agenda, many studies have been undertaken to enhance the understanding and practice of sustainable nance. The recent review of sustainable nance by Cunha et al. ( 2021 ) exempli es this observation, as the authors found that the extant literature on sustainable nance to be excessively fragmented , which makes it dif cult to identify what constitutes the eld and what differentiates it from traditional nance .

nodes.question: What does the study extend from Cunha et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: The study extends Cunha et al.'s review on sustainable finance to provide insights that were limited in their manual and qualitative review of a small literature corpus.
nodes.paragraph: In this regard, this study signi cantly extends Cunha et al. S ( 2021 ) review on sustainable nance to uncover the insights that they were not able to provide due to the inherent limitation of their manual and qualitative review of only a small corpus of the literature. Speci cally, this study sheds light on the performance analysis andscience mapping of the entire corpus of sustainable nance research using a bibliometric analysis, wherein the former unpacks the publication trend, the top articles and contributing journals, authors, institutions, and countries, and the methodological choices and research contexts, whereas the latter reveals the major themes and topics underpinning the intellectual structure of the eld. In doing so, this study will contribute enriching insights that answer six research questions (RQs) that are typically reveal through bibliometric reviews (Donthu et al., 2021b ,2021c ; Kumar et al., 2021a ,2021b ,2021c ; Rao et al., 2021 ), and thus, provide a more accurate representation of the state of sustainable nance research as a whole as opposed to the piecemeal representation that emerges from a sample of the eld, as in the case of Cunha et al.

nodes.question: What are some of the research questions explored in the review?
nodes.answer: The research questions include publication trends, influential articles and journals, top contributing authors and institutions, methodological choices, major themes, and future research directions in sustainable finance.
nodes.paragraph: ( 2021 ): RQ1. What is the publication trend for sustainable nance research? RQ2. Which are the most in uential articles and top contributing journals for sustainable nance research? RQ3. Which are the top contributing authors, institutions, and countries for sustainable nance research? RQ4. What methodological choices and research contexts exist for sustainable nance research? RQ5. What are the major themes and topics for sustainable nance research? RQ6. What are the future research directions for sustainable nance research? The insights from this review can be used in several useful ways. First, both new and sea- soned researchers in sustainable nance can gain an overview and up-to-date understanding of its publication trend to gauge its interest in the scienti C community over time (RQ1). Second, prospective authors can identify key literature (articles, journals) (RQ2), potential collaborators (authors, institutions, countries) (RQ3), as well as methodologies and contexts (RQ4) for sustainable nance research through this review. The same applies for policy mak- ers and industry practitioners who wish to identify experts for consultancy, key literature to inform decisions, as well as methodological and contextual guides for applied research.
